St. Sergius of Radonezh

Saints

St. Sergius of Radonezh

Period
1314–1392 (source account)
Region
Rus
Titles / vocation
Monastic
Commemoration
September 25

Introduction

St. Sergius is remembered as a monastic founder and abbot of Radonezh. The OCA account relates his family, early formation, community, and repose in 1392. It includes miracles and traditions about his influence on the Church and society. Those episodes remain part of the identified hagiographic narrative, while related historical lessons provide additional context for medieval Rus.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Baptized Bartholomew, St. Sergius grew up near Rostov and Radonezh. After his parents’ death, he and his widowed brother Stephen built a forest church dedicated to the Trinity.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “Bartholomew”

Life and notable events

The settlement became a community. St. Sergius was ordained, worked alongside the brethren, and developed common monastic life. The published life also recounts his blessing of Dmitry before Kulikovo.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “1354”

Sister Ioanna’s monastery account emphasizes how reluctant Sergius was to accept ecclesiastical honors. It says that he accepted priestly ordination and leadership of his own monastery only reluctantly and refused the office of Metropolitan of Moscow. The account links the growth of other northern monasteries to the work of his disciples.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Sister Ioanna, Saint Sergius of Radonezh; paragraph on disciples and ecclesiastical office

Death and martyrdom

He appointed his disciple Nikon to lead the community and reposed peacefully on September 25, 1392.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “Nikon”

Writings and legacy

His Trinity foundation and the communities associated with his disciples shaped northern Russian monasticism.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “disciples”

The original wooden Trinity church burned and was replaced by a white stone church in 1422. Sister Ioanna’s account connects St. Andrei Rublev’s iconographic work, including the famous Trinity icon, with that later church. It also relates the discovery of Sergius’s relics during construction and the tradition of their incorruption. These are parts of the monastery’s account of his subsequent veneration.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · Sister Ioanna, Saint Sergius of Radonezh; the stone church, Rublev, and the discovery of relics
